knowledge_checks.title: Active Recall: 1.1.2
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. Which statement correctly orders analysis stages and pairs a stage with a suitable tool class?
knowledge_checks.body: Select staged analysis path and tool pairing.
hints: Use the concept from this learning objective only.
knowledge_checks.explanation: Stages structure the workflow; tools serve named stages. Opening software, reversing order, or collapsing explore with inference skips staged analysis.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: Aim → data → clean/explore → analyse → communicate; EDA tools in explore.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Tool-shopping without stages, reversed order, or EDA equals inference.

choices.label: A sensible path runs from defining the aim through obtaining data, cleaning/exploring, analysing (infer or predict), to communicating results. Exploratory work sits in clean/explore and pairs with summary statistics and exploratory visualisations (or data-wrangling scripts).
Analysis stages are finished once a notebook is opened and packages loaded; tool choice replaces staged planning.
Communicate results first, then obtain data, then define the aim so stakeholders see output early.
Clean/explore and final inference are the same stage because any plot automatically completes both.

knowledge_checks.title: Checkpoint: 1.1.2
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. You are running a reserves data analysis. Which statement is correct?
knowledge_checks.body: Order stages, place EDA, pair a tool; refuse tools-without-stages.
hints: Use the concept from this learning objective only.
knowledge_checks.explanation: EDA sits inside clean/explore with appropriate tools. Package load or plots alone do not complete inference or communication stages.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: Ordered stages with EDA in explore; tools serve stages.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Equating package load or plots with finished staged analysis.

choices.label: Main stages: define aim → obtain data → clean/explore → analyse → communicate; exploratory work sits in clean/explore. That stage pairs with summary statistics and exploratory visualisations. Opening a notebook and loading packages does not finish the staged path.
Reserves analysis begins and ends in clean/explore because once plots are drawn the inference stage is complete.
The analysis is complete when R or Python packages load successfully; stage order is optional after that.
Communicate findings before defining the aim so reserves output reaches stakeholders without delay.
